name: Skrillex
notes: The brostep architect whose pop-crossover work belongs to this lane. Three tempo bands are documented — 140 for dubstep/brostep, 100-110 for the moombahton/trap crossovers, 126-130 for the house-facing material — and the modelled one is 140, because it is the only band the entry gives a drum grammar for: "at 140 the kick lands on 1 and the snare on 3 with the hats filling 16ths — the half-time grammar that makes brostep feel like a 70-BPM record". So `halfTime` is true and the snare is on `halftime_3`; the other two bands are named here rather than averaged in, since the compendium's rule is that rhythmic families are picked, never blended. ⚠ INFERRED: the entry states 140 as a single number, not a band, so the ±2 of playing room around it is a generator requirement rather than a reading — nothing above 140 is documented for him at all — and it is the same width this section's other point-tempo entries use (Deadmau5 at 128, Darude at 136). The model still extends `dance-pop` despite overriding the lane's four-on-the-floor spine, because the entry documents a four-on-the-floor mode of his own — "126-130 for the house-facing material, four-on-the-floor with a clap on 2&4" — and the volume's assignment notes place him here outright: "Skrillex and Diplo were verified against `pop-2020s` and are absent from it, so both are written up here and both are taken." `future-bass` is a related genre, not the parent. "His post-hardcore background shows in the fill density and the abrupt full-stop transitions", which is the high hat fill density, the 32nd-weighted rolls and a drop-out probability at the top of this section. Harmony is subordinate to sound design — a static tonic, with the pop-facing records using a bright modal-major loop to carry the guest vocal — so the families are few and the harmonic rhythm is `vamp`-weighted. His single most influential pop-lane device is authored in the melody: on the crossover records "a chopped, pitched guest vocal in the drop where the growl bass would be", hence the chopped-vocal timbre and the riff-loop structure. No `bass808` block: the identity is an LFO-modulated mid-range growl plus a sub sine, which is a played bass part, and authoring the 808 would have deleted it. ⚠ The research marks the harmony `[LOW-CONF]` and calls the tempo/drum grammar dubstep and electro-house convention; both marks are repeated here, and all velocities and densities are INFERRED. ⚠ **`chords.harmonicRhythm` re-weighted (2026-08-17, harmony variety floor).** The entry's harmony line is "minor-mode and modal with a static tonic; ... the pop-facing records use a bright modal-major four-chord loop to carry the guest vocal", and the engine's `vamp` value is *one* chord held for the whole clip (`generators::chords`: "One chord for the whole pattern") — so weighting `vamp` at the top rendered a **one**-chord bed the research nowhere describes. The chord motion the entry states is now carried by `1_per_bar` (the pair over a 2-bar cell) and `2_bars_per_chord` (the pair over a 4-bar cell), with `vamp` kept as the minority for the held reading. The static tonic and the four-chord loop are both the entry's, so the three rates are weighted evenly rather than one of them being chosen for him. ⚠ The split between those two rates is **INFERRED** — the entry names the device, not its rate.
